claims: certificate/s12_lower_3.9716.txt is a plain weighted-point certificate in Evan Daniel's format that s(12) >= 9929/2500 = 3.9716: side 15886400/4000000, D = 4000000, W = 9985226, 4,996 distinct positive-weight points, exactly D4-symmetric, total weight 119787760/9985226 = 11.9964996..., below 12 by 34952/9985226, so every closed unit square in [0, 9929/2500]^2 capturing weight at least one excludes twelve unit squares from any square of side below 9929/2500 (README.md, verification/summary.json).

Evan Daniel's verify, vendored unchanged from evand/square-packing 0e76d9fe and built with overflow checks, accepted it with arguments CERT 12 96000 10 0 over all 39,765 bins covering [0, 45] degrees with checked D4 symmetry, least captured weight 9985226/9985226 = 1 at bin k = 39531, exit 0, 2,167.12 s wall on 10 threads of an Apple M4 Max (verification/logs/rust.log).

Ryu Sungjoon's indep_scan.cpp, from squarepacker/s12-lower-bound 7a96bec3 with only its include line changed, accepted it with arguments CERT 96000 1000000000000000 12 over all 96,000 bins covering [0, 90] degrees with no symmetry assumed, least captured weight 9985226/9985226 at bin k = 39531, exit 0, about 626.45 s wall on one thread, run concurrently with the Rust check (verification/logs/cpp.log).

Two negative controls made by verification/replay.py --controls: W doubled with every numerator unchanged, refused by both checkers at the single bin 39531 with capture exactly 1/2 (Rust exit 4, a partial run with no verdict; C++ exit 1, NOT VERIFIED), and the last point removed with the declared count kept, refused by both parsers with exit 2 (verification/controls/).

The two checks share the certificate, the weighted closed-cover theorem, the rational angle net N = 96000 and the shrink mechanism; the README calls them separately written implementations, not method-distinct proofs, and producer evidence, and says no independent replay, review, Lean replay or parent-core interval replay was done. It claims no optimality and no new technique, and credits the new certificate instance to unnir (Numaro), building on Levy, Evan Daniel and Ryu Sungjoon and the Burns and Massaccesi framework; it says Numaro Autonomous Research (agentic autonomous autoresearch) assisted the work.
